subject: What we purge by default: request vs answer treatment
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick clar: what gets purged by default?

Hi Kimberly / Marissa —

Thanks for taking the call earlier. BrightBank legal & security asked us to get a concise list of what Redwood purges automatically vs what remains for debugging/audit. Could you confirm what we should expect out-of-the-box for: 

- Raw requests / user inputs
- Model-generated outputs / completions
- Streaming fragments / intermediate buffers
- KV cache / session artifacts
- Attachments (uploads) and user files
- Audit telemetry / trace logs

We need this in writing for our risk team and to map to our contract (we're especially interested in EU residency and evidence of deletion for customer data). Also: what customer-level controls exist to shorten retention (API flags, tenant settings, Dedicated/Private options)?

If you have a one-pager or brief we can circulate to our security reviewers that would be ideal.

Appreciate it —
Elena
Director, Cloud Security
BrightBank

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick clar: what gets purged by default?

Elena —

Thanks for the note. Short answer below, followed by a few operational notes and next steps. Attaching a short one-pager (redwood-retention-summary-onepager.pdf) with the same bullets for your auditors.

Default retention (hosted API customers, account-level defaults):
- Raw requests (user inputs): retained for 30 days by default. These are treated as sensitive by policy and are eligible for earlier erasure on customer request.
- Model-generated outputs (final completions): retained for 90 days by default for debugging and quality monitoring, unless the customer opts out.
- Streaming fragments (intermediate partial tokens): considered ephemeral; by default not persisted beyond 7 days and are only retained long-term if explicitly finalized and stored by the user or application.
- KV cache & session artifacts: session state (KV cache) is short-lived — default TTL 7 days; if session is pinned/archived by the application it becomes subject to the outputs retention window (90 days) unless the tenant changes it.
- Attachments / uploaded files: stored in customer-scoped object storage and follow the same TTL as the request that referenced them; default 30 days for files tied to ephemeral requests, longer (configurable) for artifacts explicitly archived by the customer.
- Audit/telemetry/trace logs: operational telemetry and audit trails are retained separately for compliance and incident investigation. Default retention is 365 days for audit logs, though subset exports for billing/metrics are kept longer; deletion of customer-visible artifacts does not remove audit entries needed for platform integrity unless under legal/contractual erasure orders.

Operational notes:
- Region/residency: Accounts with EU residency pin their artifacts to EU regions; deletion operations are executed in-region and evidence manifests show EU data locations.
- Erasure/POC: Customers can request erasure via the Console > Data & Privacy panel or the Erasure API (/v1/erase) — we produce a deletion manifest within 48 hours (manifest includes object ids, timestamps, and region).
- Opt-out controls: we support a per-request "no_store=true" flag and an account-level default to disable retention of requests/outputs for customers on hosted plans. Dedicated and Private deployments can set custom TTLs at the tenant level.
- Exceptions: for legal holds, investigations, or specific SLA-ed audit requirements we may retain copies until the hold is released; we document and notify customers about holds.

Next steps: I can share the short one-pager and our erasure runbook (attached) for your security team. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute tech session to walk through the deletion manifest sample and show the Erasure API call.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightbank.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clar: what gets purged by default?

Adding a few clarifications from product/ops side — Elena, important to call out for integration planning: 

- Streaming vs finalized outputs: If your app opens a streaming session but never calls the finalize/store endpoint (or doesn't set a persistence flag), the fragments are purged automatically after the ephemeral window. If your integration explicitly stores increments (e.g., saving interim transcripts), those saved entries follow the outputs retention TTL.
- Attachment handling: uploads are stored in a per-tenant store. You can opt to use your own S3/GCS (via our Private/Dedicated connectors) so file residency and lifecycle rules are enforced by you.
- Encryption & KMS: For Dedicated/Private accounts we support tenant-managed keys (HSM/KMS). If you require evidence of key destruction as part of a full data disposal, that's a separate operational runbook we can walk you through.
- API/Console controls: two practical levers we recommend for BrightBank pilots: (1) account default no_store=true for non-production envs, (2) set outputs TTL=30 days for production via tenant settings. Both are reversible and documented in the Console settings page (see drive link).

Happy to run a short proof-of-concept to show the erasure manifest and the traceable deletion entries (helps auditors).

Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Privacy & Data Lifecycle | Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightbank.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clar: what gets purged by default?

Elena — thanks for the question and Kim/Marissa for the detailed replies. Quick summary and proposed action items for BrightBank: 

Summary (short):
- Default: requests = 30 days; outputs = 90 days; streaming fragments ephemeral (7 days); audit logs = 365 days.
- Controls: per-request no_store; account-level retention overrides; Dedicated/Private tenant TTLs and tenant-managed KMS.

Proposed BrightBank next steps:
1) We will share the one-pager and the erasure runbook (attached).
2) If you want EU-only residency + 30-day TTL for production, we'll draft a short SOW amendment (ops + legal).
3) Schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough showing the Erasure API and a sample deletion manifest.

Please confirm which of the 3 next steps you'd like us to kick off. If you want the SOW path (#2) we'll loop in sales & legal.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Security Integrations | Redwood Inference
